item.research_question: How does the addition of Hafnium (Hf) in varying amounts (x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.42) to CoCrFeNi high entropy alloys affect the microstructure, phase composition, thickness, and diffusion mechanisms during boronizing and siliciding processes?
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting (2.1 × 10–6 mbar, 700 mbar Ar, 5 re-melts) followed by powder pack boronizing/siliciding using Ekabor II™ (90% SiC, 5% B4C, 5% KBF) at 1000 °C for 5 h in an electrical box furnace
item.test_conditions: Surface treatment at 1000 °C for 5 h; characterization via XRD (Cu-Kα, 20–80°, 1°/min), SEM, and EDS; cross-sectional analysis of samples cut in the middle
key_findings: The combined thickness of the silicon-rich layer and boride layer (SL-1 + BL) decreased from 70 µm for CoCrFeNi to 63 µm (CoCrFeNiHf0.1), 20 µm (CoCrFeNiHf0.2), and 15 µm (CoCrFeNiHf0.42).
The thickness of the transition/diffusion zone (DZ) increased with Hf content: 60 ± 4 µm (CoCrFeNi), 50 ± 3.5 µm (CoCrFeNiHf0.1), 97 ± 9 µm (CoCrFeNiHf0.2), and 126 ± 6 µm (CoCrFeNiHf0.42).
XRD analysis identified the boride layer (BL) as containing Ni2Si, FeB, Fe2B, Co2B, and Cr5B3 phases.
In CoCrFeNi, Si atoms accumulated close to the BL but did not penetrate the substrate, whereas in CoCrFeNiHfx alloys, Si atoms penetrated through the Ni-rich Ni7Hf2 phase.
The microstructure transformed from single-phase FCC in CoCrFeNi to FCC + Ni7Hf2 (x=0.1) and finally to FCC + C15 Laves phases (x=0.42).
Cr-B rich precipitates (Cr5B3) were observed in the BL and DZ of CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNiHf0.1, but in CoCrFeNiHf0.2 and CoCrFeNiHf0.42, they were detected only in the DZ.
The eutectic structure in CoCrFeNiHf0.42 has lamellae with a distance of about 0.01 µm, which accelerates B diffusion.
item.mechanism: Hf addition promotes the formation of Ni-Hf rich phases (Ni7Hf2 and C15 Laves) and fine eutectic structures; these phases act as channels for Si diffusion into the substrate, while the Cr-B rich layer at the interface hinders further Si transport. The fine eutectic microstructure in Hf-containing alloys accelerates B diffusion due to short diffusion distances and dominant grain/phase boundary diffusion, leading to a thicker diffusion zone but a thinner boride layer.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work.
quotes: Increasing the amount of Hf in the alloys resulted in a decrease in the combined layer thickness, which was measured for CoCrFeNi, CoCrFeNiHf0.1, CoCrFeNiHf0.2, and CoCrFeNiHf0.42 to be 70 µm, 63 µm, 20 µm, and 15 µm, respectively.
In contrast, the thickness of the transition zone/diffusion zone increased with more Hf in the alloys.
The added Hf results in the formation of the Ni-Hf phases (Ni7Hf2/Laves), which may facilitate and become the channel for Si to diffuse inwards.
